description: The brokers' Java runtime: heap by pool and after GC, garbage collection time share and pauses, allocation rate, threads, direct/mapped buffers and file descriptors. Kafka is sensitive to long GC pauses (ISR shrinks, session timeouts).

panels.description: Current heap usage of the fullest selected broker relative to -Xmx. Sawtooth between 30 % and 90 % is normal for G1; look at 'after GC' for the real pressure.
panels.title: Heap used (max broker)

panels.description: Live data that survived the last collection, relative to -Xmx. This is the real memory pressure: above 80 % the JVM collects constantly and risks OutOfMemoryError.
panels.title: Heap after GC (max broker)

panels.description: Share of wall-clock time the busiest selected broker spends in stop-the-world GC (concurrent cycles excluded). Healthy < 2 %; > 10 % hurts latency.
panels.title: GC pause time share

panels.description: Live JVM threads on the selected brokers (max). Kafka uses a fixed number; a steadily growing count is a leak.
panels.title: Threads

panels.description: Open file descriptors relative to the limit on the fullest broker. Every segment file and connection uses one; Kafka needs a high ulimit.
panels.title: File descriptors

panels.description: Time since the most recently restarted selected broker started. A small value explains under-replicated partitions and cold caches.
panels.title: Uptime (min broker)

panels.description: Heap in use, committed by the JVM and the configured maximum (-Xmx) per broker. With -Xms = -Xmx (Strimzi default when both are set) committed stays flat.
panels.title: Heap used / committed / max

panels.description: Heap usage per memory pool (young/eden, survivor, old generation), stacked, for the selected brokers. The old generation should drop after mixed/old collections; if it only grows, live data is growing.
panels.title: Heap by pool

panels.description: Heap still occupied after the last collection relative to the maximum heap, per broker. The single best signal for heap sizing: alert above 80 % for several minutes.
panels.title: Heap after GC

panels.description: Bytes allocated in the young generation per second (eden) and promoted to the old generation. Kafka should allocate modestly; high promotion rates lead to frequent mixed/old collections.
panels.title: Allocation and promotion rate

panels.description: Seconds per second spent in each collector, i.e. the share of time the JVM is collecting. G1 'Concurrent GC' runs alongside the application and is shown dashed — it costs CPU, not latency.
panels.title: GC pause time share per collector

panels.description: Average duration of a collection per collector (time spent ÷ collections, per interval). Young pauses should stay below the G1 target (MaxGCPauseMillis, e.g. 20 ms); multi-second 'Old Generation' pauses are full GCs and can expire broker sessions.

targets.expr: sum by (kafka_broker, gc) (rate(jvm_gc_collection_seconds_sum{kafka_cluster="$kafka_cluster",kafka_broker=~"$kafka_broker",gc!~".*Concurrent.*"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (kafka_broker, gc) (rate(jvm_gc_collection_seconds_count{kafka_cluster="$kafka_cluster",kafka_broker=~"$kafka_broker",gc!~".*Concurrent.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Average GC pause

panels.description: Number of collections per second per collector. Many young collections are cheap; any 'Old Generation' collection with G1 means a full GC (bad).
panels.title: Collections per second

panels.description: JVM threads by state, summed over the selected brokers. Many BLOCKED threads indicate lock contention; deadlocked threads are shown in red when present.
panels.title: Thread states

panels.description: Off-heap buffers: 'direct' (network I/O buffers, bounded by MaxDirectMemorySize) and 'mapped' (memory-mapped index files — they grow with the number of segments and count against the container memory limit!).
panels.title: Direct and mapped buffers

panels.description: Class metadata (Metaspace) and JIT code cache. Stable after warm-up; continuous growth means a class-loading leak.
panels.title: Non-heap: metaspace and code cache

panels.description: CPU cores used by the broker process (JVM view, includes GC and JIT threads). Compare with the container limit on Kafka Pods & Nodes.
panels.title: Process CPU

panels.description: Open file descriptors per broker (segments, indexes, sockets) and the process limit.
panels.title: Open file descriptors
